name: Virginia

teen.nightLimit: Under 18: no driving midnight to 4 a.m., except to/from work, supervised school or civic activity, with a licensed parent/adult in the front seat, or emergency
teen.passengerLimit: Permit: no more than one non-family passenger under 18 (DMV parent guide says under 21). License, under 18: one passenger under 21 in the first year unless a licensed parent is in the front seat; after one year, up to three under 21 in limited situations
teen.phone: Under 18: no cell phone use at all, hands-free included, except emergency while lawfully stopped or parked. All drivers: no hand-held device since Jan. 1, 2021 ($125 first, $250 second or in a work zone)

bac.under21: 0.02 (Va. Code 18.2-266.1; one-year license loss, $500 minimum fine or 50 hours community service)

notes: Knowledge exam (DMV): part one 10 sign questions, all must be correct; part two 30 general questions, 24 to pass (80%). questions/pass above are the two parts combined (10+30, 10+24). An older DMV page listed 25/20 for part two.
Exam offered in Spanish and many other languages; translators not allowed for offered languages. After three failures, a driver education classroom course is required before retesting.
Supervisor: licensed driver 21 or older beside the learner, or 18 or older if parent, legal guardian or sibling.
Reckless driving (Va. Code 46.2-862): 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph anywhere.

Move over: highways with at least four lanes, two in the same direction; change to a non-adjacent lane or slow with due caution; since 2023 covers any stationary vehicle with hazard lights, flares or warning signs (DriveSmart Virginia). No fixed mph reduction.
School bus: divided-highway exemption needs a physical barrier or unpaved area (HB409 summary, 2026); statute 46.2-859 text not retrieved; no question written.
Insurance minimum 50/100/25 for policies issued or renewed from Jan. 1, 2025; $500 uninsured motor vehicle fee ended July 1, 2024.
